verses.zh: 你们要赞美耶和华！因歌颂我们的　神为善为美；赞美的话是合宜的。
verses.en: Praise the Lord,for it is good to sing praises to our God.Yes,[NOTE:1] praise is pleasant and appropriate.
notes: Psalm 147. The psalmist praises the Lord for he is the sovereign ruler of the world who cares for the needs of his covenant people.
verses.commentary:
147:1-6 This first strophe (Ps.
147:1-6), like Psalm 146, lists several characteristics of God which can be
ascertained by His acts (this Psalm is post-exilic).

- for Israel

- builds up Jerusalem

- gathers her outcasts (i.e., exiles, cf. Isa. 11:12; Ezek. 39:28)

- for the needy

- heals the broken hearted (possibly refers to repentant Israel in exile, cf. Ps. 51:17,18)

- supports the afflicted (i.e., often used of faithful followers)

- brings down the wicked

(1) foreign nations

(2) unfaithful covenant partners

- against paganism (i.e., astral idolatry, cf. Ezekiel 8)

- counts the number of stars (Gen. 1:16; Isa. 40:26, i.e., stars are not gods, cf. Ps. 8:3)

- calls them by name (i.e., controls them)

- YHWH is abundant in strength (cf. Isa. 40:26e)

- YHWH has infinite understanding (BDB 108, cf. Isa. 40:28)

"becoming"

"beautiful"

"fitting"

This ADJECTIVE (BDB 610, KB 657) can mean

- beautiful ‒ Sol. 1:5; 2:14; 4:3; 6:4

- fitting, appropriate when used of praise to God ‒ Ps. 33:1; 93:5; Prov. 17:7

147:4b "He gives names to all of them" The naming of something in the ANE demonstrates authority
over it (i.e., Adam naming the animals, cf. Gen. 2:18-20).

147:5b Notice both lines of poetry in v. 5 may be allusions to Isa. 40:26,28. The chapter as a
whole extols the greatness of YHWH.

verses.zh: 耶和华建造耶路撒冷，聚集以色列中被赶散的人。
verses.en: The Lord rebuilds Jerusalem[NOTE:1] and gathers the exiles of Israel.

verses.zh: 他医好伤心的人，裹好他们的伤处。
verses.en: He heals[NOTE:1] the brokenheartedand bandages their wounds.
notes: For location see Map5-B1; Map6-F3; Map7-E2; Map8-F2; Map10-B3; JP1-F4; JP2-F4; JP3-F4; JP4-F4.

verses.zh: 他数点星宿的数目，一一称他的名。
verses.en: He counts the number of the stars;he names all of them.

verses.zh: 我们的主为大，最有能力；他的智慧无法测度。
verses.en: Our Lord is great and has awesome power;[NOTE:1] there is no limit to his wisdom.[NOTE:2]

verses.zh: 耶和华扶持谦卑人，将恶人倾覆于地。
verses.en: The Lord lifts up the oppressed,but knocks[NOTE:1] the wicked to the ground.
notes: Heb “to his wisdom there is no counting.”
verses.commentary:
147:6 "to the ground" This can be
understood in several ways.

- the defeated enemy bowing to the ground

- a circumlocution for death/Sheol

SPECIAL TOPIC: WHERE ARE THE DEAD?

verses.zh: 你们要以感谢向耶和华歌唱，用琴向我们的　神歌颂。
verses.en: Offer to the Lord a song of thanks.[NOTE:1] Sing praises to our God to the accompaniment of a harp.
verses.commentary:
147:7-11 As the first strophe began
with "praise" (Piel IMPERATIVE), this one (Ps. 147:7-11) begins with "singing."

- sing ‒ BDB 777, KB 854, Qal IMPERATIVE

- sing praises ‒ BDB 274, KB 273, Piel IMPERATIVE

The object of this singing is YHWH and His great acts.

- as sustainer of creation and the normal cycles of nature (cf. Ps. 104:10-17; this is usually attributed to Elohim)

- clouds

- rain

- plant growth

- food for animals (cf. Ps. 104:27b; 136:25)

- He does not trust in

- negative (cf. Ps. 33:16-17)

(1) military power (i.e., the horse)

(2) strength of men (lit. legs)

- positive (He does trust in)

(1) those who fear (see

SPECIAL TOPIC: FEAR [OT]) Him

(2) those who wait on His lovingkindness (see

SPECIAL TOPIC: LOVINGKINDNESS [hesed])

verses.zh: 他用云遮天，为地降雨，使草生长在山上。
verses.en: He covers[NOTE:1] the sky with clouds,provides the earth with rain,and causes grass to grow on the hillsides.[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “sing to the Lord with thanksgiving.”
verses.commentary:
147:8 "the heavens" See
SPECIAL TOPIC: HEAVEN

147:9b The UBS Text Project (p. 1176)
mentions a cultural proverb which asserted that ravens do not feed their young
well (cf. Job 38:41), but here it is asserted that the compassionate provider
God does!

It may also be significant that the raven (BDB 788) was
considered an unclean bird (cf. Lev. 11:15) but God still cares for them!

verses.zh: 他赐食给走兽和啼叫的小乌鸦。
verses.en: He gives food to the animalsand to the young ravens when they chirp.[NOTE:1]

verses.zh: 他不喜悦马的力大，不喜爱人的腿快。
verses.en: He is not enamored with the strength of a horse,nor is he impressed by the warrior’s strong legs.[NOTE:1]

verses.zh: 耶和华喜爱敬畏他和盼望他慈爱的人。
verses.en: The Lord takes delight in his faithful followers[NOTE:1] and in those who wait for his loyal love.
notes: Heb “he does not desire the strength of the horse, he does not take delight in the legs of the man.” Here “the horse” refers to the war horse used by ancient Near Eastern chariot forces, and “the man” refers to the warrior whose muscular legs epitomize his strength.

verses.zh: 耶路撒冷啊，你要颂赞耶和华！锡安哪，你要赞美你的　神！
verses.en: Extol the Lord, O Jerusalem.Praise your God, O Zion.
verses.commentary:
147:12-20 This third strophe (Ps.
147:12-20) also starts off with IMPERATIVES of praise.

- praise ‒ BDB 986, KB 1387, Piel IMPERATIVE

- praise ‒ BDB 237, KB 248, Piel IMPERATIVE

He is worthy of praise because of His covenant fidelity (esp. Leviticus 26;
Deuteronomy 27-30) towards Israel (i.e., Jerusalem. . .Zion).

- strengthens the fortifications of Jerusalem (i.e., gate bars)

- blesses

- the children of the city (i.e., health, their number)

- the people inside the city (TEV)

- brings peace to the land

- provides a good crop

- controls the weather (Ps. 147:16-18) so as to sustain agricultural abundance (i.e., covenant promises, cf. Ps. 147:19)

- His special relationship (i.e., revelation) to the descendants of Abraham, Isaac, Jacob

SPECIAL TOPIC: MORIAH, SALEM, JEBUS, JERUSALEM, ZION

147:14b "the finest of wheat" This is imagery for agricultural abundance (cf. Ps. 81:16)
because grain was such a staple of the ANE diet.

verses.zh: 因为他坚固了你的门闩，赐福给你中间的儿女。
verses.en: For he makes the bars of your gates strong.He blesses your children[NOTE:1] within you.

verses.zh: 他使你境内平安，用上好的麦子使你满足。
verses.en: He[NOTE:1] brings peace to your territory.[NOTE:2] He abundantly provides for you[NOTE:3] the best grain.

verses.zh: 他发命在地；他的话颁行最快。
verses.en: He[NOTE:1] sends his command through the earth;[NOTE:2] swiftly his order reaches its destination.[NOTE:3]
notes: Heb “the one who sends his word, the earth.” The Hebrew term אֶרֶץ (ʾerets, “earth”) is an adverbial accusative; one must supply a preposition before it (such as “through” or “to”) in the English translation.
verses.commentary:
147:15 God's word is personified as
running rapidly (i.e., going into all creation, cf. Ps. 19:1-6). In Hebrew thought God's word
was a creative power (cf. Genesis 1). Once given, it would accomplish its
purpose (cf. Isa. 45:23; 55:11).

verses.zh: 他降雪如羊毛，撒霜如炉灰。
verses.en: He sends the snow that is white like wool;he spreads the frost that is white like ashes.[NOTE:1]

verses.zh: 他掷下冰雹如碎渣；他发出寒冷，谁能当得起呢？
verses.en: He throws his hailstones[NOTE:1] like crumbs.Who can withstand the cold wind he sends?[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “the one who gives snow like wool, frost like ashes he scatters.”

verses.zh: 他一出令，这些就都消化；他使风刮起，水便流动。
verses.en: He then orders it all to melt;[NOTE:1] he breathes on it,[NOTE:2] and the water flows.
notes: Heb “Before his cold, who can stand?”
Heb “he sends his word and melts them.”

verses.zh: 他将他的道指示雅各，将他的律例典章指示以色列。
verses.en: He proclaims his word to Jacob,his statutes and regulations to Israel.
verses.commentary:
147:19 "words. . .statutes. . .ordinances"
See
SPECIAL TOPIC: TERMS FOR GOD'S REVELATION.

147:20b "they have not known them"
God's revelation was a special gift. It was meant to be lived out as a witness
to the nations. Israel failed in this! See

SPECIAL TOPIC: YHWH ETERNAL REDEMPTIVE PLAN.

The UBS Text Project rates this phrase as "C" (considerable doubt). It
recommends it as over against the LXX, Peshitta, NEB, "he does not let them know." This difference is

- MT, NASB ‒ ידעום ‒ בל

- LXX, NEB, REB ‒ ידיעם ‒ בל

147:20c The Psalm closes as it began—"Hallelujah"!

DISCUSSION QUESTIONS

This is a study guide
commentary which means that you are responsible for your own interpretation of
the Bible. Each of us must walk n the light we have. You, the Bible, and the
Holy Spirit are priority in interpretation. You must not relinquish this to a
commentator.

These discussion questions are provided to help you think
through the major issues of this section of the book. They are meant to be
thought provoking, not definitive.

- How do you explain Ps. 145:6,8-13 focusing on "all men" and Psalm 147 focusing on Israel (esp. Ps. 147:19-20)?

- Why is Ps. 147:4 so theologically significant in an ANE setting?

- How is Ps. 147:7-9 related to Leviticus 26 and Deuteronomy 27-30?

- God's sustaining providence described in Ps. 147:16-18 provides nature with consistent patterns.
How did this affect the development of the "scientific method" in western culture?

- Does Ps. 147:20 imply that God does not share Himself or His revelation with Gentiles?

verses.en: He has not done so with any other nation;they are not aware of his regulations.Praise the Lord!
